questions.sub_text: Your skin type affects how products work—choose yours for personalized recommendations.

optionMap.name: Normal - Balanced, not too oily or too dry
Combination - Oily in some areas, dry in others

whyWeAsk.text: Here's a quick way to find out!
whyWeAsk.heading: What's Your Skin Type?

list.title: ✨ Oily Skin
list.description: If your forehead, nose, and cheeks feel greasy and look shiny a few hours after washing, you likely have oily skin.

list.title: 💧 Dry Skin
list.description: If your skin feels tight, rough, or flaky, especially after washing, you likely have dry skin.

list.title: ⚖️ Combination Skin
list.description: If your forehead and nose (T-zone) get oily, but your cheeks stay dry, you have combination skin.

list.title: 🌿 Normal Skin
list.description: If your skin feels balanced—neither too oily nor too dry—throughout the day, you have normal skin.

questions.text: What does your acne look like?
questions.sub_text: Select all that apply to get the best treatment for your skin.

whyWeAsk.text: Here's a quick way to find out!
whyWeAsk.heading: What's Your Acne Type?

list.title: Blackheads
list.description: Small, dark clogged pores caused by trapped oil and dead skin.

list.title: Whiteheads
list.description: Tiny white bumps formed when pores get blocked with oil and bacteria.

list.title: Small Bumps
list.description: Red, inflamed pimples that don't have pus but feel tender.

list.title: Pus-Filled Pimples
list.description: Swollen red spots with a white or yellow center filled with pus.

list.title: Big Boils
list.description: Large, painful lumps under the skin caused by deep inflammation.

questions.text: Where do you mostly get pimples?
questions.sub_text: Acne location helps identify the root cause. Select all that apply.

whyWeAsk.text: Where your breakouts appear can give clues about your skin’s needs and overall health. Understanding these patterns helps us recommend skincare that works better for you while gently addressing any underlying factors.
whyWeAsk.heading: Why Acne Location Matters

questions.text: How often do you get new pimples?
questions.sub_text: This helps us track acne severity.

optionMap.name: Only after a reaction
optionMap.sub_text: (e.g., food, skincare, weather)

list.title: 🗓️ Daily
list.description: If you wake up with new pimples almost every day, or notice fresh breakouts forming consistently, your skin experiences acne very frequently

list.title: 📅 Once a Month
list.description: Do your pimples tend to appear around the same time every month? You might notice them just before an important event or as part of a regular cycle

list.title: 🔄 Once in 3 Months
list.description: If you see breakouts only a few times a year, like during weather changes or after long periods of clear skin, your acne is occasional

list.title: 🧴 Reaction to Skincare, Food, or Makeup
list.description: If your breakouts appear after trying new skincare, makeup, or eating certain foods, your acne may be triggered by external factors

list.title: ✅ None
list.description: If you rarely or never get pimples, you likely don’t experience acne

whyWeAsk.heading: How to Tell What Your Pimple Feels Like

list.title: Itchy
list.description: Feels irritated and makes you want to scratch. This can happen more in humid weather or after sweating.

list.title: Painful
list.description: Feels sore or tender. It may hurt when you touch it or even on its own for a few days.

list.title: No Sensation?
list.description: If your pimple doesn't itch or hurt, that's normal too. Some pimples appear without any discomfort.

questions.sub_text: Dandruff can contribute to acne, especially on the forehead and scalp areas.

optionMap.name: Yes
optionMap.sub_text: I notice white flakes on my scalp or hair.

optionMap.name: No
optionMap.sub_text: I don't see any flakes.

optionMap.name: Not sure
optionMap.sub_text: I haven't checked or don't know.

whyWeAsk.heading: How to Tell If You Have Dandruff
whyWeAsk.text: Dandruff appears as small white or yellowish flakes on your scalp, hair, or even shoulders. It may cause itching, dryness, or redness on your scalp. If you often see flakes on dark clothing or experience an itchy scalp, you might have dandruff. Checking your scalp in good lighting or after brushing your hair can help you notice it. If you're unsure, gently scratching your scalp with clean fingers may reveal tiny flakes.

questions.sub_text: Hormonal fluctuations play a major role in acne—let’s assess if they may be a factor for you.

optionMap.name: PCOS/PCOD
optionMap.sub_text: I have irregular periods, or extra facial/body hair

optionMap.name: Menopause
optionMap.sub_text: My periods are irregular or have stopped due to age

optionMap.name: Puberty
optionMap.sub_text: I’m a teenager or recently underwent body changes.

whyWeAsk.text: Hormonal changes can significantly impact skin health and acne formation.

questions.sub_text: Diet plays a key role in skin health—certain foods may trigger or worsen acne.

optionMap.name: High in sugar
optionMap.sub_text: I eat sweets, desserts, or sugary drinks often.

optionMap.name: High in refined carbs
optionMap.sub_text: I eat a lot of white rice, bread, pasta, or packaged snacks.

optionMap.name: Oily & fried food
optionMap.sub_text: I regularly eat deep-fried or greasy food.

optionMap.name: Processed/junk food
optionMap.sub_text: I eat fast food, chips, or packaged meals often.

optionMap.name: Balanced diet
optionMap.sub_text: I eat home-cooked meals with fresh veggies, proteins, and whole grains.

whyWeAsk.heading: How to Identify Your Diet Type

list.title: 🍫 Love sweets?
list.description: If you have desserts, sugary snacks, or drinks often, pick High in Sugar.

list.title: 🍞 Carb-heavy meals?
list.description: If you eat a lot of rice, bread, pasta, or packaged snacks, choose High in Refined Carbs.

list.title: 🍟 Fried food fan?
list.description: If deep-fried or greasy food is a regular part of your diet, go with Oily & Fried Food.

list.title: 🍔 Fast food often?
list.description: If you eat processed meals, chips, or packaged food frequently, select Processed/Junk Food.

list.title: 🥗 Mostly home-cooked?
list.description: If fresh, balanced meals make up most of your diet, choose Balanced Diet.

list.title: Pick what best describes your daily habits, not occasional treats!

questions.text: Do you have any digestive issues?
questions.sub_text: Gut health impacts skin—digestive issues can be a root cause of  acne.

optionMap.name: Acidity
optionMap.sub_text: I have a burning sensation in the stomach or throat.

optionMap.name: Gas, Bloating, or Heaviness
optionMap.sub_text: My stomach feels full, tight, or uncomfortable.

optionMap.name: Constipation
optionMap.sub_text: It is hard to pass stool or takes a long time in the toilet.

optionMap.name: Incomplete Motion
optionMap.sub_text: I still feel full after going to the toilet.

optionMap.name: None of the above
optionMap.sub_text: My digestion is fine.

whyWeAsk.heading: Understanding Digestive Issues
whyWeAsk.text: Gut health is strongly linked to skin health. Digestive issues can manifest as skin problems. Let us know what applies to help us better understand your needs.

list.title: Acidity
list.description: Burning in the stomach or throat, often after eating spicy or oily food. May come with sour burps or discomfort when lying down.

list.title: Gas, Bloating, or Heaviness
list.description: Stomach feels full, tight, or swollen, even with little food. You may burp more or feel uneasy after meals.

list.title: Constipation
list.description: Hard, dry stools that are difficult to pass or happen less often than usual.

list.title: Incomplete Motion
list.description: Feeling like you haven't fully emptied your bowels, even after using the toilet.

questions.text: Have you had any recent health issues?
questions.sub_text: Significant changes in health can disrupt hormones and metabolism, influencing your skin.

optionMap.name: Surgery
optionMap.sub_text: I had a recent surgery or medical procedure.

optionMap.name: Major illness
optionMap.sub_text: I was diagnosed with or recovering from a serious illness.

optionMap.name: Weight change
optionMap.sub_text: I've gained or lost a lot of weight recently.

optionMap.name: Recent fever or infection
optionMap.sub_text: I had a high fever, or viral infection.

whyWeAsk.heading: Why We Ask
whyWeAsk.text: We understand that life events like illness, surgery, or weight changes can impact your body in many ways. We ask this to respect your journey and ensure your skincare routine supports you through every phase, making your skin feel its best.

questions.text: How often do you drink or smoke?

whyWeAsk.heading: Why We Ask
whyWeAsk.text: Drinking and smoking can affect your skin over time. If you do either, even occasionally, it’s helpful for us to know so we can recommend skincare that works best for you. There’s no judgment—just a better way to understand your skin’s needs.

questions.text: How often do you feel stressed in a week?
questions.sub_text: Stress can lead to hormonal imbalances and inflammation, contributing to acne flare-ups.

optionMap.name: 0-1 days
optionMap.sub_text: I rarely feel stressed.

optionMap.name: 2-3 days
optionMap.sub_text: I feel stressed sometimes.

optionMap.name: 4-5 days
optionMap.sub_text: I feel stressed often.

optionMap.name: 6-7 days
optionMap.sub_text: I feel stressed almost everyday

whyWeAsk.text: Look back at your week and think about how often you felt tense, overwhelmed, or anxious. Did stress affect your mood, sleep, or focus most days, or just once in a while? If you felt calm and relaxed most of the time, you may fall into the lower range. If stress was a daily experience or impacted your energy, appetite, or thoughts frequently, you may be in the higher range.
whyWeAsk.heading: How to Track Your Stress
